title: A relationship call that establishes nothing keeps the open-time source capture, and the byte question it was expected to raise turns out to be already answered by the comparison it replaces
code_state: crates/litchi-opc/src/rel.rs only, plus one unit test and one integration test file; no public signature, error type, limit, dependency or output byte changed; no new unsafe
reason_codes: change 0628 reported this as the one litchi-opc finding it deliberately did not fix, because keeping the capture looked like it would move published bytes from the canonical serialization to the source spelling
the corpus measurement shows 2,189 of 2,216 relationships members are spelled differently from canonical, so the byte consequence would fire on 98.78% of the corpus if it existed; it fires on none

the reason is structural, not a corpus accident: try_write_preserved's non-pristine branch compares the canonical serialization it just built against the same open-time capture and, on equality, takes PreservationAction::Copy of the source archive entry, which is exactly what the pristine branch takes; the full-writer route materializes pristine members before write, so it emits the canonical serialization on both legs

the call establishes nothing: add_relationship's occupied entry returns the established relationship without replacing it, so the value the capture is a proof of is unchanged, and the relationship built from the arguments was discarded unobserved

value identity is proved two ways: 6,281 reuse publications over 334 fixtures are byte-identical to their seam-only baselines on both legs with an empty cross-leg diff, and four in-crate integration tests pin the same equality on a fixture whose members are provably non-canonically spelled

accepted_evidence.spelling_gap: probe/src/rels_spelling.rs over 336 OOXML fixtures: 2,216 source relationships members, 27 canonical, 2,189 differing, 6,281 internal relationships, largest member 43 Relationship elements
accepted_evidence.value_identity: probe/src/reuse_publish.rs over 336 fixtures: 2,190 collections, 6,281 reuse calls, each publishing twice through the owned-source route; 6,281/6,281 byte-identical to the seam-only baseline, 0 differing, 0 unexpected growth, 96 baseline and 260 reuse refusals of two typed kinds in identical counts on both legs; per-fixture rolling SHA-256 digests make the cross-leg diff a complete oracle and it is empty
accepted_evidence.ordinary_route: probe/src/docx_route.rs over 63 .docx-family fixtures through the documented Package::open -> document_mut().add_paragraph_with_text -> to_stream route: 52 published, 141 source relationships members, 118 kept and 23 moved on both legs, cross-leg diff empty
accepted_evidence.call_counts: callgrind isolation pairs, N=1 and N=11, differenced and divided by 10, four scenarios per leg on ConditionalFormattingSamples.xlsx; exact-symbol call counts for try_to_xml_bytes, verify_authored, rels_uri, add_relationship, get_or_add and reuse_candidate
accepted_evidence.allocations: probe/src/reuse_counts.rs with a counting global allocator, five (fixture, owner) pairs, per-phase allocation and byte counts, published byte count and SHA-256 identical on both legs
accepted_evidence.instructions: the same isolation pairs' whole-run Ir totals, with two seam-only control scenarios that execute no changed code to quantify code-layout and allocator drift
accepted_evidence.timing: probe/src/reuse_iters.rs --timing, 500 samples per block, 20 warmup, blocks ordered A1 B1 B2 A2 for 1,000 samples per leg, plus four before-only blocks for the A/A floor in the same window; two scenarios and one re-run window, all on CPU 22 with binaries staged outside the Cargo target directories

accepted_costs.widened_scope: the change applies to every add_relationship call naming an already-taken identifier, not only to get_or_add's reuse path; that call was already a silent no-op because the occupied arm never replaced anything, but a caller who believed add_relationship always invalidated is now wrong
accepted_costs.skipped_refusals: on the preservation route a pristine member no longer runs try_to_xml_bytes or verify_authored, so an allocation failure while building a discarded buffer, and an audit failure on a discarded serialization, no longer refuse; this is change 0593's already-recorded behaviour class and needs roughly 62,500 relationships in one member, against a measured corpus maximum of 43
accepted_costs.error_ordering: on the full-writer route a pristine member is serialized and audited in materialize_pristine rather than in PublicationPlan::from_package, so if two members would both fail the audit the variant is the same but the message may name a different one; no bytes are emitted in either case
accepted_costs.instruction_counts: instructions rank work, not latency; callgrind counts rep movsb per byte and runs SHA-256 in software; one deterministic run per leg, with the two control scenarios bounding the recompile drift at 2,018 to 7,813 instructions
accepted_costs.timing_resolution: the work removed is 0.08% to 0.45% of the scenario's instructions while the measured p50 deltas are 0.69% to 1.40%, so the timing is not fully explained by the work removed and this host's floor cannot separate the two; no timing claim is made

known_gaps.reported_regression: the drawing scenario's first timing window shows +11.70% mean and +230.79% p99 on the after leg; the per-block breakdown attributes it to one contaminated block (a 31 ms sample, 9.96 ms p99) while that block's own p50 stayed at 1,543 us and all four A/A blocks stayed under 1,715 us at a host load average of 39; re-running the same scenario in a second window gives -1.40% p50 and -1.39% mean against a floor under 0.05%
known_gaps.ordinary_format_routes: measured only for DOCX, where the change saves nothing because the save rebuilds the document part into a fresh BlobPart that never carried a capture; for XLSX, PPTX, XLSB and litchi-ooxml-common the answer is an audit of every production call site, not a measurement: litchi-xlsx has no production get_or_add or relate_to call site, litchi-pptx's materialize_presentation is unreachable from an opened package, and litchi-xlsb's writer authors from OpcPackage::new()
known_gaps.reachable_but_unmeasured: litchi-xlsb/src/cell_values/resources.rs:242 (ensure_styles_part) and :337 (the shared-strings attach) guard on the part existing rather than the relationship, so a source carrying a dangling styles.bin or sharedStrings.bin relationship would reach a reusing get_or_add on a capture-bearing collection; neither was measured
known_gaps.source_backed: litchi-opc/src/source_backed.rs has its own relationship serialization and publication path; this change touches neither and no source-backed scenario was measured
known_gaps.corpus_bound: 336 OOXML fixtures, 2,216 relationships members, 6,281 reuse calls; the soundness argument does not depend on the corpus, which is the oracle that it holds in practice

withheld: any registered speedup, throughput, cold-cache, physical-I/O, concurrency-scaling, real-producer or cross-platform result
